title: Install or recover Annals
summary: Install, update, verify, or recover the user-owned Annals deployment or its physically separate decisions library, including guarded Clockwork handoff.
use_when: The user-owned macOS Annals and Annals Usage binaries, configuration, content-addressed release, Clockwork binding, library, or spool must be installed, updated, or recovered.
An explicitly authorized fresh-state replacement must preserve uncompleted backlog and rollback as one generation.
The dedicated Annals decisions library and independent `annals/decisions-inbox` binding must be provisioned, updated, maintenance-held, or recovered.
do_not_use_when: The task is ordinary use or administration of an already installed library or inbox.
Source development or Git release publication is the intended outcome.
A destructive fresh-state cutover has not been explicitly authorized.
outcome: A verified complete installed Annals release or dedicated decisions-library generation with its exact independent Clockwork binding, matching configuration, library/spool identity, Nucleus selector, and rollback state.
effects: Stages and atomically selects a complete content-addressed release containing Annals, Annals Usage, runners, configuration, and provider documentation.

Registers an immutable Clockwork definition for `annals/inbox`, proves any selected prior digest resolves to the complete exact current Annals release definition before disabling or replacing it, establishes maintenance, migrates the library, and atomically switches the binding only after the exact release is ready.

During legacy system migration, the child deployer returns an inert rendered definition under maintenance; the outer migration durably commits the permanent user-state root before it registers or selects that definition.

Removes or restores a legacy LaunchDaemon or LaunchAgent only when its complete plist, owner, and mode match the exact Annals rendering; migration also proves the system service absent before removing its files or clearing maintenance, and additional launchd keys are foreign.
With `--fresh-state`, replaces the library and spool together, imports uncompleted backlog in lane order, and retains the prior generation for rollback.

The decisions provisioner creates the separate database with its immutable decisions role and requires any existing state to retain that role after its supported schema check; it owns only that database's fresh bound spool, config, logs, backups, and `annals/decisions-inbox` definition, shares the Annals update lock, and never changes `annals/inbox`.

Before opening decisions state or selecting its schedule, the provisioner requires existing mutable control files and both fixed logs to be operator-owned private regular single-link files; absent logs are created privately and symbolic or hard-linked targets fail closed.
With `--keep-maintenance`, records and retains an Annals-owned decisions maintenance hold for an outer cutover; a later successful invocation clears only that matching owned hold.
A failed pre-commit cutover restores captured program, service, configuration, library, and spool state according to the supported procedure.
authority: Annals owns its installed programs, library, spool, schedule requirements, configuration, migration, maintenance, domain result, and recovery.

Clockwork owns the immutable executable definitions, selected bindings, non-overlap enforcement, launchd projections, and activation process history for `annals/inbox` and `annals/decisions-inbox`; it never owns Annals job or corpus success.
Nucleus remains separately authoritative for Codex execution and authentication and is not stopped or replaced by an Annals deployment.
success: Installed Annals and Annals Usage versions and help surfaces match the selected release.
Library migration and statistics checks, spool status, the exact Clockwork binding, Nucleus readiness, and deliberate Annals and usage canaries pass as applicable.
Maintenance is cleared only after the complete cutover commits and backlog processing is intentionally resumed; an explicitly requested decisions handoff instead reports maintenance still engaged.
failure_and_recovery: Do not remove maintenance, edit spool receipts, or replace library files manually after interrupted deployment; inspect and use the documented recovery procedure.

A measured closed inbox storage gate does not itself reject a deployment, but `storage_probe_failed` can reject status inspection and insufficient physical space can fail release staging, backup, migration, or rollback writes.
A failed ordinary update restores the previous captured generation before work resumes.

A legacy migration failure before the outer commit registers no definition and restores the system installation; a committed interruption or unproved system-service retirement retains maintenance and its handoff for idempotent completion.

A decisions provisioning failure before binding commit restores the captured config, database, and exact attributable prior schedule state; unprovable restoration leaves only the decisions library maintenance-gated and retains recovery material.
A fresh-state cutover is destructive to the active generation and requires explicit retained rollback material and backlog verification.
privacy: Installed library, spool, backups, configuration, logs, and Nucleus output may contain complete private sources and model context.
Deployment must preserve private user ownership and permissions across both current and rollback generations.
does_not_authorize: Running `annals/release.sh`, which commits, tags, and pushes.
A fresh-state replacement without explicit destructive-operation authority.
Clearing user data as storage remediation, or lowering or disabling the inbox storage reserve, without the user's explicit consent for the exact target and scope.
Disabling a same-key Clockwork binding or removing a same-label plist or installed pathname without proving its exact Annals release or rendered-file identity.

Concurrent same-user direct Clockwork mutation of `annals/inbox` during deployment or migration; ownership inspection and binding mutation are not a compare-and-swap, and a detected change fails closed behind the maintenance recovery gate.
Using decisions-library authority to mutate the primary `annals/inbox` binding, the primary library or spool, Nucleus, release bytes, or a foreign `annals/decisions-inbox` definition.
Deleting prior generations, backups, logs, or retained failed envelopes.

consumers.statement: An authorized local macOS operator may install, update, verify, or recover the user-owned Annals and Annals Usage deployment, or separately provision its dedicated decisions library and schedule.
This operation is not source development, Git publication, routine library administration, implicit fresh-state replacement, or storage cleanup.

preconditions.statement: Candidate Annals and Annals Usage binaries have passed the product gate, and the caller supplies absolute candidate binary, Nucleus binary, Nucleus socket, and compatible Clockwork paths with enough physical capacity for staging and recovery writes.

An ordinary update requires every selected `annals/inbox` definition to match the complete current Annals release and executable contract field for field; legacy system migration requires the binding to be absent or disabled with no selected digest before commit.
Fresh-state replacement additionally requires explicit destructive authority, retained prior-generation rollback material, and a verified uncompleted-backlog import and recovery plan.

Decisions provisioning requires a complete format-four content release whose independently hashed provisioner and both decisions templates are unchanged; any selected prior decisions definition must match that dedicated state and a fully verified Annals content release field for field.

Existing decisions config, database sidecars, spool control and identity files, maintenance state, and fixed logs must be operator-owned private regular files with exactly one hard link; the database must carry the immutable decisions role.

inputs.statement: Primary deployment accepts absolute Annals, Annals Usage, Nucleus binary, Nucleus socket, and Clockwork binary paths plus optional --fresh-state; decisions provisioning instead accepts one exact absolute content-release root, Nucleus socket, Clockwork binary, and optional --keep-maintenance.
The deployer does not accept release publication, arbitrary cleanup, manual receipt editing, implicit data deletion, or Nucleus replacement as installation inputs.

outputs.statement: Success selects a complete format-four content-addressed release containing both binaries, the release-local inbox runner, primary and decisions Clockwork templates, decisions config and provisioner, legacy ownership-check template, configuration, provider bundles, and a verified compatible library and spool generation, then binds the exact definition digest.

Decisions provisioning success returns one body-free ok/data envelope containing the absolute config path, persistent library ID, exact Clockwork key and definition digest, selected/enabled booleans, maintenance state, and content release ID.
Verification exposes installed versions, Nucleus health, Annals statistics and inbox status, and Annals Usage diagnostics; deliberate execution and usage canaries remain boundary-dependent checks.

data_semantics.statement: An ordinary update migrates and preserves the active library and spool; fresh state replaces them together and imports uncompleted backlog in preserved lane order.
Maintenance is an Annals deployment boundary distinct from operator pause and storage gate; it clears only after the complete cutover commits.
A measured closed storage gate does not itself reject deployment, while an unreadable probe or insufficient physical capacity can fail required inspection or writes.

identity_and_units.statement: Product versions, provider releases, content-addressed release identity, current selector, Clockwork keys `annals/inbox` and `annals/decisions-inbox`, immutable definition digests, persistent decisions library ID, library schema, and library/spool rollback generations are distinct identities.
Storage checks and reserve comparisons use filesystem bytes; freshness and service checks are observations made during the selected deployment.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: The current selector changes only after the staged release, configuration, library migration or replacement, spool, provider bundles, and service checks form one complete candidate generation.
Post-cutover checks inspect the newly selected installed commands and current service state rather than a retained readiness snapshot.
No deployment-duration, service-availability, rollback-retention duration, or disk-capacity service-level objective is promised.

access.statement: The supported boundary is the repository-owned macOS deployers operating the current user's private primary installation or physically separate decisions state and only their respective Clockwork keys.
The operation does not own or replace Nucleus, publish Git state, delete recovery material, or grant direct library and spool editing.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Deployment stages and registers an inactive exact-release definition, establishes maintenance, proves and disables only an exact current-release Clockwork selection and quiesces any owned legacy LaunchAgent, captures recovery state, performs supported migration or authorized replacement, switches selectors and exactly one Clockwork binding, verifies, then clears maintenance.

The former-system migration is the exception to pre-commit definition registration: its child renders an inert definition under maintenance, and the outer migration durably records the target state as permanent before registering and selecting it. RunAtLoad remains maintenance-gated until the system service is proved absent and exact legacy retirement completes.

Rollback restores the exact prior definition only when that binding was enabled, or restores the prior owned legacy LaunchAgent, never both. A previously absent or disabled binding remains disabled without transient activation; its inactive selected digest may remain the candidate digest. If exclusive restoration cannot be proved, Annals leaves unproved scheduler state untouched, keeps maintenance, removes its public selectors, and retains private recovery material.
An ordinary pre-commit failure restores the captured program, service, configuration, library, and spool generation before work resumes.
Fresh state treats library and spool plus uncompleted backlog as one rollback generation; credentials remain forward-only and outside binary or database rollback.

Decisions provisioning stages fresh state off-path, binds a fresh spool, engages maintenance before publication, registers the candidate inactive, drains only an enabled proved prior, backs up before migration, verifies inbox and feed readiness, switches only `annals/decisions-inbox`, then clears only its own gate unless --keep-maintenance was requested.
The primary `annals/inbox` binding and general library stay available throughout decisions provisioning; both deployment paths serialize through Annals' shared update lock.

operational_limits.statement: The supported deployers are per-user macOS Clockwork installations, require absolute inputs, serialize on one Annals update lock, stage one complete generation, and need enough physical capacity for release, backup, migration, and rollback artifacts.
Deployment authority never implies fresh state, data cleanup, reserve reduction, prior-generation deletion, or service work outside Annals.
No maximum installed-state size, deployment time, retained-generation count, or service downtime bound is promised here.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Annals and Annals Usage package versions, provider releases, library schema, Nucleus protocol, and installed generation are checked as separate axes and cut over together where the package owns them.
Library changes use only supported migrations or explicit fresh state; provider selectors follow the same release generation as their executables for rollback.
No cross-release installation support window, migration horizon, or deprecation period is promised.

reliances.statement: Primary deployment checks a separately owned Nucleus binary, socket, compatibility, authentication readiness, and requester boundary; decisions provisioning records the supplied absolute Nucleus socket but leaves its current readiness to the outer cutover. Neither stops or replaces Nucleus.

Deployment and unattended inbox processing rely on Clockwork schedule contract 1 for immutable definition registration, one selected binding, non-overlap, activation history, and its launchd projection.
Annals promises no launchd availability or wake-up latency beyond the observations exposed by Clockwork.
